title: Restore playing what was playing before a TTY session change
line: Music and radio that were playing before you switch to another TTY or user session start playing again when you come back.
explanation: When the session is switched away, the session loses access to the audio device, so players stop or pause their stream, and nothing in Plasma started them again on return. Players often react before logind's session change reaches Plasma, so only looking at what is playing at that moment would miss them. The media controller daemon (kded mpris module) now watches the logind session's Active property, remembers players that were playing or stopped within two seconds before the session became inactive, and calls Play on those that are not playing when the session becomes active again.

commits.message:
kded/mpris: resume players that were playing before a session switch

Switching to another TTY or user session takes the audio device away,
so players stop and stayed stopped when coming back. Remember the ones
that were playing and resume them when the session is active again.

BUG: 513642

media.caption: Before: a radio stream is playing (tray tooltip: Middle-click to pause).
Before: after switching to another session and back, the radio stays paused.
After: the same radio stream playing before the switch.
After: back from the other session, the radio is playing again by itself.

review.text: Watching logind's Active property in the kded mpris module, which already knows every player, is a reasonable place for this wish, and it only resumes players that were playing, leaving ones that were already playing alone. The two-second 'stopped just before' window is a heuristic (a pause by hand right before switching gets resumed), but there is no cleaner signal for players that lose their device first. Verified only with a fake logind and fake player, not a real VT switch with PipeWire, which maintainers may ask for.
